Article Title: Portronics Zeno L Mini air compression leg massager: Price, features and more
Article Text:
Portronics Zeno L Mini air compression leg massager: Price, features and more

Portronics has launched the Zeno L Mini, a cordless air compression leg massager designed to help users relieve leg fatigue, soothe muscle tightness and support post-workout recovery. Combining adjustable compression, multiple massage modes and cordless operation, the device offers a convenient way to enjoy a personalised massage experience at home.Portronics Zeno L Mini comes in a sleek black finish with a compact wraparound design that fits securely around the leg. Its Velcro fastening allows users to adjust the fit, while the compact form factor makes it easy to store and carry. The design makes it suitable for use after workouts, during relaxation time or after long hours on the feet.The Zeno L Mini offers six massage modes – Calf, Thigh, Upper Arm, Forearm, Recovery and Targeted, allowing users to choose a mode based on their preferred massage area and requirement. It also provides two pressure levels – Low and High, giving users greater control over compression intensity, along with 10-minute and 20-minute timer options for customised massage sessions.The detachable control unit has dedicated buttons for power, pressure, massage mode, and timer settings, making it easy to adjust the massage experience.The air compression system works through an inflate, compress, and release cycle, delivering controlled compression around the legs.The device is powered by a 2,000mAh rechargeable battery and is claimed to deliver up to 75 minutes of runtime on a single charge. The device supports Type-C charging for easy and convenient recharging, while its cordless design provides greater freedom of movement, allowing users to use the massager comfortably without being connected to a power source.The Portronics Zeno L Mini comes with an MRP of Rs 5,999 and is currently listed at Rs 2,849 on Portronics.com. The product comes with a 12-month warranty and can also be purchased from Amazon.in, Flipkart.com, and other leading online and offline retail stores across the country.
Article Summary: Portronics Zeno L Mini is a cordless air compression leg massager. It is designed to relieve leg fatigue, soothe muscle tightness and support post- workout recovery. The device is powered by a 2,000mAh rechargeable battery and is claimed to deliver up to 75 minutes of runtime on a single charge.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg tells investors Meta’s AI investments are accelerating every part of the business; and to IRS, Meta says: Our AI data centers are an experiment that could fail
Article Text:
Meta’s AI data centers: a success for investors, an ‘experiment’ for the IRS

How Meta turned Nvidia AI chips into 'pilot models' for tax purposes

Meta's own filings warn the AI tax savings could be overturned

The tax credit's original sponsor says it was meant for people, not hardware

Mark Zuckerberg has spent two years telling investors that Meta's AI spending is paying off across Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook. When the company files its taxes, it tells the US Internal Revenue Service (IRS) a very different story. According to a New York Times report, Meta describes its AI data centers to the IRS as a large experiment that may not work.That framing lets Meta claim the Research and Experimentation Tax Credit, a break Congress created in 1981 to reward risky innovation. The payoff has been big. Meta says the credit cut its tax bill by $2 billion in 2024 and $3.9 billion in 2025, up from $700 million in 2023, the year before it started using it for data centers. The NYT found Meta is now the largest beneficiary of the credit among publicly traded companies.In its tax filings, Meta classifies its multibillion-dollar AI data centers as "pilot models." Under the rules, supplies qualify for the credit only when they are part of an experimental effort, not regular business. So Meta argues the costly chips it buys from Nvidia and others belong to an experiment and deserve the discount.The idea came from an employee overseeing the data center build-out in mid-2024, the report says. Some in Meta's finance team doubted it would survive scrutiny, since the IRS has previously rejected claims for proven, commercially available equipment. Lawyers Meta consulted pointed to a 2021 ruling that denied the credit to an Indiana shipbuilder, which held that simply building a new product isn't enough. After a few months of deliberation, Meta began tagging chips bound for AI data centers differently from those going to standard ones.Andre Shevchuck, a research tax credit specialist at advisory firm BPM, called the experimental label "kind of wild and out there."Meta's accountants appear to share some of that doubt. Since the strategy began, the company's unrecognized tax benefits, the money set aside in case tax authorities win a challenge, have climbed 45% to $18.74 billion from $12.9 billion. The first reason listed in its annual filing is uncertainty around research tax credits.Apple, Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft also report over $1 billion a year in research credits. None has flagged it as a risk to investors.Meta spokesman Andy Stone said the company invested $200 billion in R&D over five years, $57 billion of it last year, and uses incentives Congress set up for this kind of domestic investment. He called unrecognized tax benefits a mandated accounting measure of uncertainty. Meta declined to explain what makes its data centers experimental.This isn't Meta's only research credit fight with the IRS. The agency is trying to claw back $355 million after Meta counted $4.1 billion in stock options Zuckerberg exercised in 2013 as a research expense. Separately, the IRS wants nearly $16 billion over profits it says Meta shifted to the Cayman Islands.James Shannon, the former Massachusetts congressman who sponsored the credit, told the NYT it was meant to back researchers and knowledge, not manufacturing. Meta's use, he said, goes "way, way beyond" what anyone imagined.The Joint Committee on Taxation estimated the credit would cost the US government $32.1 billion in 2025. Meta alone accounts for more than a tenth of that, on a bet its CEO keeps telling investors is already working.
Article Summary: Report: Meta describes its AI data centers to the IRS as a large experiment that may not work. That framing lets Meta claim the Research and Experimentation Tax Credit. Meta says the credit cut its tax bill by $2 billion in 2024 and $3.9 billion in 2025, up from $700 million in 2023.

Article Title: H-1B Visa: US government has suspended PERMS for Infosys, TCS, Wipro and Cognizant employees: What this means for Green Card applicants, older and others
Article Text:
What is PERM and why does it matter

What does it mean for H-1B workers

The unknowns that matter most

Why the suspension matters

The US government’s decision to suspend several major technology firms, including Infosys , Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, Cognizant, HCLTech, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe, from the PERM labour certification programme could significantly delay Green Card pathways for thousands of foreign workers, particularly Indians employed on H-1B visas. The move, announced by the US Department of Labor, prevents the affected companies from filing new PERM applications and processing pending PERM cases. US officials said the action was taken over alleged misuse of foreign worker programmes and concerns about the impact on American jobs. Vice President JD Vance, who announced the action jointly with Sonderling, called H-1B workers "foreign indentured servants" and the companies "visa mills," arguing the practice has shut Americans out of the job market. An investigation was also ordered into the J-1 visa programme for research scholars at nine major universities, including Yale, Harvard, Stanford and Caltech.Workers who haven't started PERM. If their employer cannot file a new PERM application, they may have to wait before beginning the standard employer-sponsored green card route. They also cannot establish a priority date through a new PERM filing during the suspension.The priority date sets a worker's place in the green card queue. That matters especially for Indian professionals, who already face lengthy queues because of high demand and country-based numerical limits.Workers with a pending PERM. The Labor Department has said it will not process pending applications involving the named companies during the suspension. In practice, long-pending cases that were already waiting could be frozen where they stand.Workers with an approved PERM or I-140. It is unclear whether already approved labor certifications or immigrant petitions will be affected, and officials have not given guidance. Lawyers who analyzed earlier suspensions at other companies said approved PERM certifications, approved I-140 petitions and existing H-1B status were not wiped out. That may not carry over to this action, so affected workers should ask their attorneys.Visa and work status. A PERM suspension is not the same as cancelling H-1B visas. It does not by itself change a worker's current status.It’s important to note that this decision of the US government does not cancel the existing H-1B visa s. Also, the employees presently working on a valid H-1B visa in the IS can continue to work as per their current visa approvals. But the workers relying on employer-sponsored Green Cards may face some major delays in obtaining permanent residency. Also, the workers whose PERM applications are pending, or who were planning to start the process, could witness delay in immigration timelines.Officials have not said how long the suspension will last or how the companies can get it lifted. Under Labor Department regulations, an initial suspension during a fraud investigation can run up to 180 days and be extended while the investigation is unresolved, so lawyers warn employers not to assume processing resumes automatically.For H-1B holders, time is a concern. Under federal law, H-1B workers can generally extend beyond the six-year limit only if a PERM was filed at least a year before that limit is reached. Workers who cannot get a PERM filed may need to consider other options, such as changing employers. This is general background, not guidance specific to this suspension, and an immigration attorney should advise on individual cases.The action marks one of the most significant recent restrictions on the employment-based Green Card process for major technology companies. While workers can continue to hold H-1B status, the freeze effectively blocks a crucial pathway to permanent residency for employees of the affected firms, raising uncertainty for thousands of foreign professionals awaiting Green Cards.
Article Summary: The US government has suspended the PERM labour certification programme. The move could significantly delay Green Card pathways for thousands of foreign workers, particularly Indians employed on H-1B visas. US officials said the action was taken over alleged misuse of foreign worker programmes and concerns about the impact on American jobs.

Article Title: Anthropic launches free AI-powered security scanner for open-source software projects
Article Text:
How OSS Scanner from Anthropic works

Anthropic spent several weeks testing

How to join

AI giant Anthropic has introduced a free vulnerability-scanning service for open-source software projects, using its latest Claude models to identify security flaws and generate bug reports as the company expands its efforts to apply artificial intelligence to cybersecurity. The new service, called OSS Scanner, is an opt-in programme that offers periodic security scans to eligible open-source projects at no cost. Anthropic said the initiative draws on lessons from its vulnerability research efforts under Project Glasswing and is designed to help maintainers discover and fix software weaknesses before attackers can exploit them.According to Anthropic, language models have become significantly more capable at finding software vulnerabilities. The company said AI systems have improved from detecting fewer than 20% of vulnerabilities on a key academic benchmark early last year to finding more than 85% this year.OSS Scanner's output is fully model-generated, with no human review or triage. Anthropic said this allows faster and more frequent scans but means some reports may be incorrect or invalid. Each report includes a self-contained reproducer and an explanation of the vulnerability.Where possible it also traces when the bug was introduced, and it offers a candidate patch when one is available.Anthropic will keep sending human-verified reports through its existing coordinated vulnerability disclosure process, especially for projects that lack resources to triage reports themselves. OSS Scanner is an optional fast track for maintainers who want reports as soon as they are generated. It is separate from Claude Security, Anthropic's general-access code scanning and patching product for enterprises.Anthropic spent several weeks testing the pipeline with dozens of open-source projects. The first disclosures contained hundreds of bug reports, including several vulnerabilities that could be chained into unauthenticated remote code execution exploits.In one validation exercise, expert penetration testers who review Anthropic's disclosures checked 97 critical and high-severity findings across 48 projects. Of these, 85 (88%) met the bar for the disclosure process. Of the other 12, 11 were real but duplicated known issues or other scan findings, and one was a false positive. Anthropic acknowledged that some maintainers have said severity ratings can be inflated, or that the scanner misunderstood a project's threat model.Maintainers who tested early versions were largely positive:* PostgreSQL: Noah Misch said several reports came with fixes the project could use nearly as they were, and that fast-track access let the team address new issues before a general-availability release.* OpenSSL Corporation: Anton Arapov said the reports, raw model output included, were as good as and sometimes better than those from people, especially when an exploit was attached.* wolfSSL: Todd Ouska said that of 74 reports, all but two were valid and five became CVEs.* HotCRP: Eddie Kohler praised the reports for their grasp of the project's complex permission model.Core maintainers of eligible projects can enroll by submitting a pull request to a GitHub repository Anthropic has set up. Eligibility follows criteria similar to OSS-Fuzz's, chiefly that a project has "critical impact on infrastructure and user security." Anthropic will decide case by case. Anthropic also pointed to two related programs: a Cyber Verification Program that gives qualifying security professionals advanced cyber capabilities with fewer blocking classifiers, and Claude for OSS, which offers free Claude Max 20x subscriptions to help fix vulnerabilities.
Article Summary: OSS Scanner is an opt-in programme that offers periodic security scans to eligible open-source projects at no cost. Anthropic said the initiative draws on lessons from its vulnerability research efforts under Project Glasswing. Each report includes a self-contained reproducer and an explanation of the vulnerability.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu to Indians who are on a visa in US: Come back; America no longer …
Article Text:
Sridhar Vembu wrote an open letter to Indians in America

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has urged Indians living and working in the US on a visa to return to India, saying many Indians who have contributed to America's technology sector are now facing uncertainty about their future there. In a post on X (formerly known as Twitter), Sridhar Vembu said that Indians had played a major role in building America's technological strength, but added that a section of the country no longer wanted them. “Indians have made a major contribution to America's technological prowess. Yet, a big part of America no longer wants us,” Vembu wrote.He also highlighted the personal cost of immigration uncertainty for Indians who have built their lives in the US after years of hard work. “Indians who are on a visa in the US face the painful prospect of uprooting the life you have built with hard work,” he said.“Let this be the birth pains of a bold new future. Come back, let's build India 🙏,” he wrote.Sridhar Vembu's comments come amid concerns among Indian professionals about their ability to work and settle in the US. Many Indian technology workers depend on employment-based visas, including the H-1B visa , while some seek permanent residency through the Green Card process.When a user asked “What exactly was the problem with India, that the brains from India built US whereas they could not do anything here”, Vembu replied:“The Chinese migrated in large numbers even as China developed.Taiwanese migrated in large numbers as Taiwan developed. Same with South Korea and before that Japan.My point is that development at a national level accompanies out migration of talent seeking better opportunities faster”.In April this year, Vembu shared an open letter addressed to Indians living in the United States. The letter then urged “brothers and sisters from Bharat” to consider returning to India and contribute to the country’s growth. In the post, Vembu reflected on his own journey to the US decades ago and acknowledged the opportunities it provided. At the same time, he pointed to changing perceptions around immigration and jobs, saying that Indians abroad are increasingly caught in broader political debates.“You may think the next election will fix this, but your choice would be between people who hate our Bharatiya civilisation and people who hate civilisation itself. That is the "hard right" vs "woke left" battle. You are mere bystanders to that conflict,” Vembu wrote.
Article Summary: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has urged Indians living and working in the US on a visa to return to India. He said Indians had played a major role in building America's technological strength, but added that a section of the country no longer wanted them. Many Indian technology workers depend on employment-based visas, including H-1B visa.

Article Title: India’s startup boom masks a growing wellbeing crisis: Study
Article Text: Nearly half of those working in India's startup ecosystem reported low levels of mental wellbeing, with employees faring worse than founders and investors, according to a new study released ahead of World Mental Health Day on October 10.The *State of Mind: The Startup Ecosystem* report found that 47.5% of respondents scored at or below its wellbeing threshold. Among startup employees, the figure rose to 54.3%, compared with 42.9% among founders, 45.2% among investors and 44.2% among other ecosystem stakeholders.The study, which surveyed 823 people across India, also found a strong link between mental wellbeing and psychological safety at work, or how comfortable people feel admitting that they are struggling.Overall, 34.8% of respondents said they felt unsafe speaking up. Among employees who felt this way, 88.3% scored low on wellbeing, compared with 26.7% of employees who felt safe acknowledging difficulties.Another finding was the gap between how people assessed their own mental health and what their wellbeing scores suggested. Of the 391 respondents who scored below the threshold, 35.3% still described themselves as thriving or doing okay.Only 15.1% reported seeking professional help.The study was initiated by Sheetal Bahl, Founder and Partner at venture capital firm Merak Ventures, and authored by Priyanka Kartari, Dr Sukhmani Pal and Dr Dilip Panniker.“To those who are part of it, it will unlikely come as a surprise how poorly the ecosystem is faring. But this study highlights some nuances, like while all groups show concerning results, it is employees who carry the largest share of stress,” Bahl said.“The silver lining is that the fixes are not rocket science – make it safer for people to speak up, give them some support, and allow them real time-off, and the wellbeing improves dramatically,” he added.The initiative is supported by study's co-authors and 1mg co-founder Gaurav Agarwal and Akshit Mathur.The report also draws attention to the business implications of poor mental health, citing industry findings that associate prolonged exhaustion with entrepreneurs leaving their businesses and employees taking more sick leave or looking for other jobs.It recommends regular anonymous wellbeing assessments, confidential support systems, training for managers and protected time off. Investors, too, have a role to play, the report suggests, by factoring wellbeing into due diligence and supporting mental health initiatives within their portfolio companies.The research used an adapted version of the World Health Organization's Five-item Well-Being Index, alongside respondents' own assessments of their wellbeing.Of the 1,040 survey submissions received, 823 were retained for analysis, including 347 founders or co-founders, 300 employees, 124 investors and 52 ecosystem supporters.The researchers cautioned that the survey was self-selected and captured responses at a single point in time. The wellbeing threshold used has not been independently validated for the adapted index, and the findings do not establish clinical diagnoses or a causal relationship between workplace conditions and mental health. The difference in wellbeing between founders and employees also narrowed after accounting for demographic factors and working hours.The report, released ahead of World Mental Health Day, calls for more sustained attention to mental health across India's startup ecosystem, particularly among employees whose difficulties may otherwise go unrecognised.
Article Summary: Nearly half of those working in India's startup ecosystem reported low levels of mental wellbeing. Employees faring worse than founders and investors, according to a new study released ahead of World Mental Health Day on October 10. Report calls for more sustained attention to mental health across the startup ecosystem.

Article Title: Google Cloud launches universal ‘Gemini Agent’ with deep app integration
Article Text:
How Google’s Gemini Agent operates

Unified Interface and API:

Omnipresent and headless deployment:

Execution in the Cloud:

Multi-agent orchestration:

Deep context:

Deep integration across Google Workspace apps

Personal Assistance:

Proactive delegation:

Team Coworker Agents:

Google Cloud unveiled the Gemini agent at its annual Gemini at Work 2026 conference, positioning the system as a universal, single digital assistant engineered to handle enterprise knowledge work, run complex code and execute multi-step workflows straight from a prompt box. According to Google Cloud, nearly 500 enterprise customers each processed over one trillion tokens in the past year alone. Furthermore, approximately 80% of all Google Cloud clients now deploy its artificial intelligence offerings, while nearly 90% of Fortune 100 enterprises actively use Gemini Enterprise. With business environments pivoting toward agentic systems, Google stated that the new Gemini agent is built around delegating end objectives rather than micromanaging step-by-step instructions.The Gemini agent is designed around six core architectural pillars.Users can chat, delegate autonomous objectives, schedule background duties, and generate code from a consolidated interface without switching between disconnected applications.The system functions across web interfaces, iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows. It integrates directly into developer command lines, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and Slack, or operates headlessly behind third-party enterprise tools.Running entirely on cloud infrastructure, the agent retains a shared memory bank and personalization graph across all endpoints. Users can initiate a job that runs for hours or days, close their computer, and return to completed deliverables without re-briefing the system.When handling complex projects, Gemini can spin up specialised, temporary sub-agents to tackle parallel or sequential tasks. It can also stand up permanent "coworker agents" assigned to specific team functions. These coworker agents receive their own dedicated email addresses (such as @agents.company.com), independent cloud storage, and role boundaries.The system retains four distinct layers of memory: session memory for active jobs; semantic memory for company documentation; procedural memory for repeatable workflows; and episodic memory to recall past interactions.Flexible multi-model routing: The agent decouples the user experience from the underlying foundation model. It dynamically routes queries to the most cost-effective and accurate engine available, navigating Google’s own Gemini family alongside Anthropic’s Claude models, with support for future private and open-source models.The agent works directly across Gmail, Drive, Docs, Slides, Sheets, Chat and Calendar through three primary modes:Knowing a user’s schedule and team relationships, the agent can coordinate across apps automatically. For example, it can assemble an attendee list from past chat threads, review calendars, and send scheduling emails without requiring manual contact entry.Built-in Workspace Intelligence identifies tasks within inbound emails, such as a manager requesting a presentation, and serves up one-click prompts allowing users to delegate the task directly to Gemini. The inbox also highlights messages based on operational importance rather than arrival time.Departments can generate artificial colleagues that show up directly in corporate directories with their own calendar and Drive storage. Team members can tag the coworker agent in Chat or add them to document comments, where the agent suggests edits and answers questions under its own identity without exposing wider personal files.
Article Summary: The Gemini agent is designed around six core architectural pillars. Users can chat, delegate autonomous objectives, schedule background duties, and generate code from a consolidated interface. The system functions across web interfaces, iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows. It integrates directly into developer command lines, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and Slack.

Article Title: Anti-aging influencer Bryan Johnson has an advice for Elon Musk; says: I hope Elon would clean up his ...
Article Text:
Shifting from wealth to 'Don't Die'

Anti-aging influencer and tech millionaire Bryan Johnson is urging the world’s richest man, Elon Musk , to reconsider their life priorities, offering pointed health advice to the tech mogul by stating that human survival should supersede financial gain. Appearing in an interview on The Axios Show, the 49-year-old entrepreneur, who reportedly spends upwards of $2 million each year in a quest to reverse biological aging, stated that society is approaching a turning point where wellness will outshine net worth.When asked what counsel he would share with Musk, Johnson expressed a desire to see the Tesla and SpaceX chief look after his physical wellbeing so he can reap the rewards of his labour:“I hope Elon would clean up his health. I mean, he’s worked so hard. He has a lot of potential to enjoy what he’s built,” Johnson said, as per Axios.Johnson also noted that he would welcome the opportunity to help President Donald Trump with his physical health, adding that world leaders frequently reach out to him for guidance and that he regularly participates in group chats with prominent tech executives and influencers.Johnson envisions a cultural transition away from traditional financial success toward his personal longevity mantra, dubbed “Don't Die”. His ultimate benchmark for success is whether future civilisations look back favorably on his pioneer work:“Will the 25th century … be like, 'thank you' in 500 years? Will they give me a head nod? That’s the goal,” Johnson remarked.“Society says making money … is the greatest trophy one can get … we are at this inflection moment as a species where we are transitioning to 'Don't Die.' What creates status and power and prestige is going to be different. And as crazy as it sounds, it may be your nighttime erections … It may be your ability to dunk a basketball at age 49. ”To guide his pursuit of biological youth, Johnson has turned his home into an advanced testing facility and gathered an enormous digital record of his bodily functions. Backed by wearables, a dedicated concierge medical squad and home diagnostic suites, Johnson is said to have amassed over 4.2 billion individual data points concerning his physiology, deploying AI software to detect trends and draw actionable conclusions.In 2023, Johnson famously swapped blood plasma with his teenage son. While the experiment benefited his elderly father, Johnson discontinued it for himself after tests indicated his biomarkers were already equivalent to an 18-year-old’s.Johnson openly documents intimate metrics with his 8 million social media followers, sharing updates on everything from sperm vitality to nocturnal erections.
Article Summary: Bryan Johnson is urging the world’s richest man, Elon Musk, to reconsider their life priorities. The 49-year-old tech millionaire believes that human survival should supersede financial gain. Johnson has turned his home into an advanced testing facility and gathered an enormous digital record of his bodily functions.

Article Title: Popular VC Paul Graham disagrees with Amazon ‘ban’ on Meta's Muse and Perplexity's Comet AI; says that blocking AI Agents will backfire
Article Text:
Amazon’s pushback against ‘outside’ AI

Renowned venture capitalist and Y Combinator co-founder Paul Graham has criticised Amazon ’s aggressive crackdown on third-party AI shopping assistants, warning that shutting out these automated agents may open the door for a startup rival to challenge the e-commerce giant’s market dominance. In multiple posts shared on X (formerly Twitter), Graham argued that consumer habits are shifting toward agentic workflows, and attempting to lock external tools out of storefronts will inevitably backfire by fueling demand for more open competitors.“Amazon banning agents is the first opportunity I've seen since Amazon was founded for a startup to create an Amazon competitor. People will want agents to buy stuff for them. It will be one of the main use cases. And they won't want to use some Amazon-supplied agent to do it,” Graham said.He framed restrictive platform policies as an open invitation for disruption, adding: “Any business that bans agents represents an opportunity for a startup to create a competitor. If they need to ban agents, it must mean people want to use them, or there would be no point. And that in turn means there's demand for a competitor that allows them.Your usage restrictions are my opportunity.”Graham’s remarks follow a series of defensive moves by Amazon to shield its marketplace from outside AI scrapers and purchasing bots.In September, Amazon confirmed it cut off Meta’s new Muse personal AI agent from shopping on Amazon.com on behalf of users. The retail titan stated that it took the step after trying unsuccessfully to convince Meta to voluntarily leave the e-commerce site out of the experience.Further, Amazon claimed it never permitted the access, noting that Meta failed to give prior notification, that Muse browse sessions do not identify themselves and that the tool appears to capture and store customer credentials, creating potential privacy and security vulnerabilities.Prior to the ban on Meta’s Muse, Amazon was in a year-long effort to block third-party agents across the board. The company filed a lawsuit against AI search firm Perplexity over its Comet browser and moved to prevent shopping agents built by Google and OpenAI from crawling its marketplace.Amazon launched Alexa for Shopping in May, an AI agent that researches products and makes recommendations.
Article Summary: Y Combinator co-founder Paul Graham has criticised Amazon’s aggressive crackdown on third-party AI shopping assistants. Graham argued that shutting out these automated agents may open the door for a startup rival to challenge the e-commerce giant”s market dominance. He framed restrictive platform policies as an open invitation for disruption, adding: “Your usage restrictions are my opportunity”

Article Title: Vi Business, Hindalco partner to deploy private network at Odisha bauxite mine

The company said the initiative aligns with its vision of building connected and intelligent mining operations while improving workforce safety and operational efficiency.The digital transformation programme also complements Hindalco's sustainability efforts. Article Title: 70% of Indian firms prioritise AI, but security concerns slow adoption: Dell study
Article Text:
More organisations move AI into production

Security remains a major roadblock

Infrastructure readiness a key concern

Businesses seek strategic technology partners

Building foundations for the next phase of AI

Around 70% of Indian organisations have made artificial intelligence (AI) a strategic priority, but concerns around security, compliance and infrastructure readiness continue to hinder adoption, according to Dell Technologies' Modern Enterprise Readiness Study 2026. The study, which surveyed 2,950 business and IT decision-makers across 35 countries including 150 respondents from India, found that AI adoption in India is accelerating as companies move beyond experimentation towards production-scale deployments.According to the report, 26% of Indian organisations now have AI or generative AI solutions running in production environments, up from 20% a year ago. The findings highlight growing enterprise confidence in AI technologies as businesses look to integrate them into core operations. However, organisations are becoming more cautious about investments. Across the Asia Pacific, Japan and Greater China (APJC) region, 72% of respondents said they would not pursue new AI initiatives without clear business outcomes and a defined risk management strategy.The report noted that enterprises are increasingly focused on translating AI investments into measurable returns rather than pursuing projects based solely on technological promise.Despite the enthusiasm around AI, security and regulatory concerns continue to be a significant challenge. The study found that 61% of Indian organisations have experienced delays or pauses in AI adoption due to security and compliance concerns. As AI systems become more deeply integrated into critical business operations and data environments, organisations are placing greater emphasis on governance, privacy and regulatory compliance frameworks.Dell said these concerns are forcing businesses to consider trust, risk management and data protection much earlier in the AI deployment process.Infrastructure preparedness emerged as another major hurdle for scaling AI initiatives.According to the study, 67% of Indian organisations believe their current data centre environments are not ready to support AI workloads at production scale. Enterprises increasingly require advanced compute, storage and networking capabilities to run AI applications effectively, creating pressure to modernise existing infrastructure.The report suggested that organisations that successfully upgrade their infrastructure foundations could gain a competitive advantage as AI adoption expands.The study also highlighted a shift in enterprise spending patterns, with nearly nine out of ten Indian organisations redirecting investments toward technology partners capable of supporting large-scale AI and digital transformation programmes. Rather than relying on individual products or point solutions, organisations are increasingly looking for partners that can provide end-to-end support across AI, infrastructure, data and security environments while delivering measurable business outcomes.Commenting on the findings, Venkat Sitaram, Senior Director and Country Head, Infrastructure Solutions Group, India, Dell Technologies, said organisations are taking a more integrated approach to transformation, where AI, infrastructure, workplace modernisation and security must work together."Organisations are looking beyond individual technologies and seeking partners that can help them navigate complexity, strengthen resilience and translate technology investments into measurable business outcomes," Sitaram said.The study concludes that while India's AI momentum remains strong, long-term success will depend on secure and modern infrastructure, clear business outcomes and strategic partnerships that can support AI deployments from planning through execution.
Article Summary: Dell's Modern Enterprise Readiness Study 2026 surveyed 2,950 business and IT decision-makers across 35 countries. It found that AI adoption in India is accelerating as companies move beyond experimentation towards production-scale deployments. However, security and regulatory concerns continue to be a significant challenge.

Article Title: LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman: When we started, we told employees, sure, go home, have dinner with family, and then open laptops to…
Article Text:
LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman says early employees got a dinner break with family, then went straight back to their laptops.

Reid Hoffman's stance on work-life balance has stayed the same for over a decade

Hoffman says early LinkedIn employees were rewarded for the long hours

Not every founder agrees with Reid Hoffman that work-life balance means losing

LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman has never been shy about how much a startup should take out of the people building it. In a clip that has resurfaced on social media, Hoffman describes the deal LinkedIn offered its earliest employees: go home, have dinner with your family, then open your laptop and get back to work. About a third of the company's early team had children, and that dinner break was close to the only time off the schedule allowed.The remarks come from Hoffman's 2014 talk at Stanford University's "How to Start a Startup" class, where he told aspiring founders that anyone chasing a balanced life is not serious about winning. More than a decade later, the work-life balance debate has only grown louder, and Hoffman's position has barely moved."If I ever hear a founder talking about, 'This is how I have a balanced life,' they're not committed to winning," Hoffman said in the Stanford session. The great founders, in his view, are the ones willing to put everything they have into the company.He repeated the point on the Diary of a CEO podcast in late 2024, calling startups "by nature dead" and saying work-life balance is simply not part of the game. In May 2025, he squeezed the same idea into a 16-word post on X: "If a founder brags about having 'a balanced life,' I assume they're not serious about winning."It crossed a million views within days.Hoffman also has little patience for people who call this culture toxic. They don't understand how startups work, he has said, and they are "just wrong". The pace comes with the job, and a founder who can't keep up eventually loses it.By Hoffman's own account, LinkedIn was the softer version. At PayPal , which he helped found earlier, dinner was served in the office so nobody had to leave. Letting people eat at home before logging back in was, by that standard, a concession.He frames the whole arrangement as a choice. Nobody is forced to join a startup, Hoffman argues, and those who do know what they are signing up for. He also points to the payoff. Microsoft acquired LinkedIn for $26.2 billion in 2016, and according to Hoffman, the roughly 100 people who joined first no longer need to work.Some tech leaders share his view. Eric Wittman, who became VSCO's CEO in 2023 and took the photo app to its first profit in 2024, has said that stress and late nights are part of rebuilding a company, and that leaders have to accept that pain rather than avoid it.The pushback has been just as loud. When Hoffman's X post went viral, 37signals co-founder Jason Fried called the take "stupid". Small Bets founder Daniel Vassallo replied that a balanced life is itself the win.Critics most often point to Netflix co-founder Marc Randolph. Randolph, Netflix's first CEO and a co-founder of seven companies, kept Tuesday evenings free for date nights with his wife for more than 30 years. On those days he left work at 5 pm, whatever was happening at the office. He has said he is prouder of staying married and close to his children than of any company he started.Research leans toward that side too. Harvard's decades-long study of adult development has found that close relationships are among the strongest predictors of long-term happiness and health.Where a founder lands usually depends on what they count as winning. Hoffman counts the $26.2 billion exit and the early employees who never had to work again. Randolph counts three decades of Tuesday evenings away from his desk. LinkedIn's dinner-then-laptop rule sits firmly at Hoffman's end of that scale, and nothing he has said since suggests he would loosen it.
Article Summary: LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman says early employees got a dinner break with family, then went straight back to their laptops. The remarks come from Hoffman's 2014 talk at Stanford University's "How to Start a Startup" class. Hoffman repeated the point on the Diary of a CEO podcast in late 2024, calling startups "by nature dead"

Article Title: She homeschools four children while running 11 AI agents: How this founder turned her home into an AI laboratory
Article Text:
Jesse Genet's homeschooling agents use OpenClaw

For Jesse Genet, running a household with four young children and homeschooling three of them could easily be a full-time job. Instead, the former Silicon Valley founder is using 11 AI agents to handle parts of her family’s education and everyday household work. Genet, a former Y Combinator founder who previously built and sold a packaging company, said she had expected to step away from technical work for several years so she could focus on her children. That changed after she began experimenting with AI agents that could build and complete tasks for her.“I feel like I've been building better things than I ever have before,” Genet said on the A16Z podcast.Genet's three older children are aged five, four and two, while her fourth child is a baby. She uses AI agents to help prepare lessons based on the homeschooling curricula she follows. Her main homeschooling agent, which she calls Sylvie, has access to the core curriculum texts, Genet's education philosophy and photos of the Montessori materials available at home. It can create lesson plans and suggest which materials to use.Genet also uses voice notes and photos to record what her children learned. An agent turns those quick updates into detailed lesson logs, helping it keep track of where each child is in the curriculum.The AI is not limited to homeschooling. Genet said she uses agents to order groceries, buy items needed for children's activities and handle other household tasks.Jesse Genet said she now has 11 agents, 10 of which use OpenClaw. She runs them on Mac Minis and uses Obsidian to store information and lesson logs. Her setup has also become increasingly autonomous. Genet said her existing agents can now create new agents themselves when they become overloaded with work.She said she wants to use AI whenever she encounters a task that takes her away from what she actually wants to be doing, such as spending time with her children.But the experiment has also shown the risks. Genet once gave an AI agent access to her email. After she mentioned struggling to send an important email, the agent interpreted it as a request for help and sent the message on her behalf. She later removed its ability to send emails.“Trust, but verify,” Genet said, describing the lesson she took from the incident.Genet said the experience reinforced the need to restrict what AI agents are technically allowed to do rather than simply telling them not to do something.
Article Summary: Former Y Combinator founder Jesse Genet is using 11 AI agents to handle parts of her family’s education and everyday household work. Her main homeschooling agent, which she calls Sylvie, has access to the core curriculum texts, Genet's education philosophy and photos of the Montessori materials.

Article Title: Bill Gates secretly credited him as a creator of Windows 1.0; forty years later Gabe Newell three months under him taught him more than his time at Harvard; lesson he has taken to the seas
Article Text:
The Windows 1.0 lesson that traveled to Sea

How Newell brought team philosophy on his superyacht

What makes Leviathan different

Gabe Newell worked under Bill Gates developing the initial version of Windows at Microsoft in his early years. Forty years ago, his name was quietly coded into a hidden screen inside a fledgling operating system that would revolutionise personal computing. Today, the Valve co-founder and gaming billionaire has brought that same ethos of recognising the contributors to his 364-foot, $500 million megayacht, Leviathan.Newell was just 23 years old when Microsoft rolled out Windows 1.0 on November 20, 1985. The MS-DOS-based release faced widespread development delays and industry skepticism, with critics initially brushing it off as “vaporware.” Behind the scenes, a core team of around 13 people was pushed to solve systemic engineering hurdles rather than stay confined to narrow job descriptions. Newell has repeatedly credited this high-intensity phase as the foundation of his managerial style, noting that just three months working under Bill Gates taught him far more than his entire education at Harvard University.That tight-knit software team left a secret calling card. Embedded inside a bitmap file was an unlisted credit roll bearing 36 names, including Newell and Steve Ballmer, which was triggered by an intricate keyboard sequence.As recounted during 40th-anniversary project retrospectives, Gates stumbled across an early iteration of the screen after punching in keys in frustration over system latency, prompting developers to make the trigger even harder to find. The hidden roster stayed undiscovered until 2022, when a security researcher reverse-engineered the original binaries, as reported by PC World.Delivered last year by Dutch shipbuilder Oceanco, the Leviathan vessel stands as an intensely personal creation for Newell. Apart from a 10-meter pool, expansive panoramic windows and a massive 5.3MWh battery system, the vessel features a sea lobby dedicated entirely to the workforce that built it.At the midships entry point, visitors encounter a full-height glass panel engraved with the names of nearly 3,000 people – spanning Oceanco naval architects, specialist craftspeople, project contractors, and crew members. In a nod to gaming culture, an Oceanco-designed Leviathan crest is etched to appear only when viewed from specific angles, an intentional design detail described by Boat International as an "Easter egg. "The main deck of the Leviathan replaces the standard formal dining hall with a communal layout accommodating up to 56 people, allowing guests and crew to eat together. The bridge deck houses a full basketball hoop and a large games room, while the sundeck includes a spa pool and space for beer pong. The oversized kitchen is engineered with modular cooking stations designed to double as an operational training academy for chefs.Beyond hospitality, Leviathan functions as a versatile mobile base for Newell’s wide-ranging ventures across deep-sea exploration, neuroscience, tooling, and artificial intelligence. Through Inkfish, his marine exploration organisation, Newell supplies resources to oceanographic researchers.Other features include an operational diving and ocean research workshop equipped with a laboratory and 3D printing equipment; an interactive gaming studio outfitted for virtual reality and holographic systems; and a soundproofed lower-deck studio that accommodates music gear, including a full drum kit, and serves as an editing bay for audio and video production.
Article Summary: Gabe Newell's $500 million superyacht features a sea lobby dedicated entirely to the workforce that built it. At the midships entry point, visitors encounter a full-height glass panel engraved with the names of nearly 3,000 people. The main deck of the Leviathan replaces the standard formal dining hall with a communal layout accommodating up to 56 people.

Article Title: ATM’s ‘dying technology’ problem may come to trouble data centres, as these engineers may increasingly ‘disappear’
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation

COBOL is running out of people

Replacing COBOL systems is not simple

COBOL skills are becoming more valuable

COBOL may be decades old, but it still powers critical financial infrastructure and 95% of ATM transactions, according to IBM. Now, as the engineers who maintain these systems age out and fewer young developers learn the language, the skills needed to keep this infrastructure running could become scarce.This could also create problems for data centers supporting financial services, where legacy systems still run on COBOL. Banks and businesses may struggle to maintain systems they can't easily replace, and the shortage of skilled engineers has existed for years. It will only get worse as experienced COBOL programmers retire.COBOL was never designed to become such a deeply embedded part of modern infrastructure. Yet 66 years after its creation, financial institutions, businesses, and governments still use it widely.The language has evolved over time. COBOL introduced object-oriented programming in 2002, while IBM has continued developing products around it. A new standard was also released in 2023. But modernising the language does not solve the shortage of people who can maintain decades-old systems.The problem is not new. Computerworld highlighted the ageing COBOL workforce in 2008 and again in 2012.In 2013, ZDNet reported that universities were avoiding teaching COBOL because it had become "uncool."Moving away from COBOL is difficult because financial systems can contain hundreds of millions of lines of code. Simply asking AI to translate that code into a newer language may not be enough.Calvin Smith, in a breakdown by YouTube channel OpenHands, said attempts to use AI agents for such work have not been particularly successful. IBM also pushed back against the idea that modernising COBOL systems is simply a matter of translating code, saying it involves "data architecture redesign, runtime replacement, transaction processing integrity, and hardware-accelerated performance."That complexity makes any transition, gradual or not, risky. In 2018, a major failure occurred when UK bank TSB shifted from one platform to another. Unable to access their accounts, the bank was then fined £48.65 million ($65.86 million) and affected millions of customers.The shrinking pool of COBOL engineers is also creating financial incentives for those with the expertise. Some jobs require several years of experience with the language and can pay between $100,000 and $150,000, with some positions offering more.The bigger question is what happens when even those engineers begin to disappear. Replacing decades of carefully maintained financial infrastructure with newer languages such as Rust would be expensive and carry significant risks.For banks and other organisations, the challenge may therefore be less about whether COBOL is old and more about whether enough people will remain who understand the systems built around it.
Article Summary: COBOL still powers 95% of ATM transactions, according to IBM. As engineers who maintain these systems age out and fewer young developers learn the language, the skills needed to keep this infrastructure running could become scarce. This could also create problems for data centers supporting financial services.

Article Title: Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ First Impressions
Article Text: At Rs 1,29,999 in India, the Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ sits firmly in Samsung’s premium tablet lineup, aimed at users who want a large-screen device for work, entertainment, note-taking and creative tasks. The Tab S12+ also marks an interesting change in Samsung’s tablet lineup. After bringing back an 11-inch model with the Galaxy Tab S11 series, Samsung has moved back to a 12.6-inch Plus model with the Tab S12+. The bigger screen gives it more room to work with, while the tablet remains noticeably smaller and lighter than the 14.6-inch Ultra.We got some time with the Galaxy Tab S12+ and our initial experience suggests that Samsung has focused on refining the formula rather than completely changing it. The tablet gets a brighter display, a newer MediaTek Dimensity 9500 processor, an S Pen in the box and support for Samsung’s laptop-like DeX experience.The first thing that stands out about the Galaxy Tab S12+ is its 12.6-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X display. It supports a 120Hz adaptive refresh rate and Samsung says the panel can reach up to 1,600 nits of peak brightness.The screen also benefits from Samsung’s Vision Booster technology, which adjusts brightness based on the surrounding lighting conditions.During our initial time with the tablet, the display looked bright and sharp, while the larger 12.6-inch panel gives the S12+ plenty of space for watching videos, browsing and working with multiple apps.The design is also quite slim. The Galaxy Tab S12+ measures 5.3mm in thickness and weighs 553 grams, making it considerably easier to handle than the larger Ultra model. Samsung has also given the tablet an IP68 rating for water and dust resistance, which is useful for a device in this price range.Performance is handled by the MediaTek Dimensity 9500 processor, which is also used in the Tab S12 Ultra. Samsung is promising gains in CPU, GPU and AI performance over the previous generation. Based on our early experience, the tablet feels fast and responsive, although the performance improvements are more evolutionary than revolutionary.The Galaxy Tab S12+ also comes with an S Pen, continuing Samsung’s focus on productivity and creativity. Users can take notes, annotate documents, sketch and use the stylus for other everyday tasks.Samsung is also positioning the Tab S12+ as a potential laptop replacement. Article Title: Jensen Huang remembers Windows early days, crediting Microsoft, says that 'Nvidia was founded because of Windows'; CEO Satya Nadella jokes: If you could just do a little transfer of...
Article Text:
Jensen Huang and Satya Nadella relive the Windows 95 days.

Windows 95 and DirectX gave Nvidia's GPUs a way into the PC

A four-year-old conversation between Huang and Nadella led to RTX Spark

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has said his company owes its existence to Microsoft's operating system. Speaking on stage at Microsoft's Windows and Surface event in San Francisco on October 7, Huang told the audience that "Nvidia was founded because of Windows," and traced a line from Windows 3.1 in 1992 to the GPUs that now power much of the AI industry.Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, sitting next to him, had a quick reply. "If you could just do a little transfer of market cap back to me," he joked, a nod to how far Nvidia's valuation has climbed. Huang shot back: "I do that every day." The conversation, hosted by Sriram Krishnan, former senior policy adviser for AI at the White House, came right after Microsoft unveiled the Surface Laptop Ultra and a range of laptops built on Nvidia's new RTX Spark chip.Huang went back to late 1992, when Windows 3.1 was showing what a personal computer could become. He admitted he had never seen a PC at the time, having mostly worked on workstations, file servers and the supercomputers used to design chips. He and his co-founders imagined a PC with 3D graphics that could play games, work as a workstation and be used to design things.Windows 95 then made it possible to connect a GPU to a PC, and DirectX, through its Direct3D API, let applications use what the GPU could do.With DirectX 8, Huang said, Nvidia and Microsoft co-invented the first programmable GPU with programmable shaders. A few steps later, that work evolved into CUDA, Nvidia's parallel computing platform."If not for Windows, there would be no GeForce," Huang said. Without GeForce, he added, there would be no CUDA, and AI researchers like Andrew Ng would not have found a computer to do deep learning on.Nadella called the story "the history of computing in some sense" and credited Huang as the most consistent voice on what accelerated computing could become. He recalled an early Azure deal to scale high-performance computing in the cloud, which led Microsoft to build the supercomputer it later offered to OpenAI. When Sam Altman asked if Microsoft had the compute, Nadella's answer was "yeah, maybe."That partnership eventually brought the two back to the PC. Huang said they discussed how to put every major tool, from Blender to Adobe and Autodesk apps, on the same machine as AI agents. "By the way, took four years," Nadella added.The result is RTX Spark, which Huang said took over 4,000 engineering years and has been tested on more than 1,200 applications. RTX Spark laptops from Asus, Dell, HP, Lenovo, MSI and Microsoft's own Surface are now up for preorder and begin shipping on October 16.As the session wrapped up, Huang summed up the relationship himself: "Windows has been with me for 34 years, it looks like it's going to be with me for 34 more."
Article Summary: Jensen Huang: "N Nvidia was founded because of Windows" He traced a line from Windows 3.1 in 1992 to the GPUs that now power much of the AI industry. Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella discussed how to put every major tool on the same machine as AI agents.

Article Title: In 2019, the research company that called now bankrupt WeWork 'most ridiculous IPO of 2019' has same 'most-ridiculous' description for Anthropic IPO, and reason is ...
Article Text:
Anthropic’s valuation expectations at the centre of concerns

A mixed track record

What the firm hasn't seen

As AI giant Anthropic moves toward a highly anticipated public listing that could value the company at nearly $2 trillion, independent research firm New Constructs has issued a scathing assessment, calling it the "most ridiculous IPO of 2026" and drawing comparisons with WeWork, whose failed public offering became one of the biggest corporate collapses of the last decade. According to a report by CNBC, the criticism carries some weight on Wall Street because New Constructs used the same description for WeWork in 2019, months before the office-sharing company abandoned its IPO plans amid investor backlash over its finances and governance. WeWork eventually filed for bankruptcy in 2023. According to a CNBC report, the research firm's latest report argues that Anthropic's proposed valuation presents an even bigger risk for investors than WeWork's offering did.New Constructs estimates that to justify a $2 trillion valuation, Anthropic would need to earn twice what Nvidia, the world's most valuable tech company, earned over its past four quarters. Nvidia's net income over that period topped $190 billion. The firm pointed to Anthropic's reported finances. According to Reuters, which cited a leaked copy of the company's prospectus, Anthropic had revenue of $4.6 billion in 2025 and a net loss of $42 billion.Those losses, along with growing competition from open-source models, led the firm to a blunt conclusion: "We don't think Anthropic has a viable business." The report argues that closed models were always going to struggle to turn a profit once open-source alternatives arrived.It also argued that the offering's purpose is not to create wealth for public-market investors but to give Anthropic's Wall Street backers liquidity. And it said Anthropic's own warning that AI could pose a "catastrophic or existential risk to humanity" is another reason for investors to stay away. The firm acknowledged Anthropic's value beyond the balance sheet. "While Anthropic offers more to society than WeWork ever did," it wrote, the $2 trillion valuation makes the IPO a far bigger risk and potentially a "far bigger rip off of US capital markets. "David Trainer, New Constructs' founder and CEO, has built a reputation as a bear on IPOs, and he has sometimes been right. WeWork had been privately valued at $47 billion when New Constructs published its report. Six weeks later, WeWork pulled its IPO amid weak demand and criticism of its financials, and it filed for bankruptcy in 2023.The firm was also bearish on Allbirds' 2021 offering. The shoe company reached a $4.1 billion valuation on its first day on the Nasdaq. Earlier this year it sold its assets to American Exchange Group for an estimated $39 million and pivoted to AI.The firm has also been wrong. Its "most ridiculous" pick for 2020 was DoorDash, which it called "similarly disadvantaged" to WeWork. DoorDash jumped on its first day of trading in December 2020, with a market cap above $60 billion, and is now worth about $83 billion. Trainer acknowledged in a 2021 CNBC interview that "crazy stuff happens" and that the firm does not always get it right. "I can't let that bother me," he said then. "I have to stay true to what I think is right."Anthropic has not made its prospectus public, so New Constructs has not seen the actual filing. The firm relied on reported figures, including from the New York Times, which reported in September that Anthropic was on pace for $100 billion in annualized revenue by the end of 2026. Anthropic said at the end of July that its annualized revenue run rate had risen sevenfold year over year to $65 billion."While we were not fortunate enough to be one of the few to whom Anthropic's S-1 was selectively disclosed," the firm wrote, the reports of leaked financials "reveal more than enough" to judge the risks.
Article Summary: Anthropic is preparing for a highly anticipated public listing that could value the company at nearly $2 trillion. Independent research firm New Constructs has issued a scathing assessment, calling it the "most ridiculous IPO of 2026" The report argues that Anthropic's proposed valuation presents an even bigger risk for investors than WeWork's offering did.

Article Title: After $6.25 billion 'gift' to Trump Accounts, Michael Dell's wife Susan Dell makes an 'appeal' to parents and grandparents, says: There is money in ...
Article Text:
Michael Dell and wife Susan Dell

What are Trump Accounts

Michael and Susan Dell donated $250 each to first 25 million Trump accounts

Michael Dell’s wife Susan Dell has made an ‘appeal’ to parents and grandparents to claim their child’s money in Trump accounts. The couple attended a press conference alongside President Donald Trump at the Oval Office celebrating the automatic enrollment of millions of American children in the ‘Trump Accounts’. “We believe in you, and we want you to dream big because we know you can make your dreams come true,” Susan Dell said adding “So parents and grandparents, please claim your child's account. These accounts are ready. They're waiting for you, and they have money in them.”The move comes months after Michael and Susan Dell committed $6.25 billion to fund “Trump Accounts” for children in the US. Announcing the donation last year, Michael Dell said: "We've seen what happens when a child gets even a small financial headstart - their world expands".Trump Accounts are new, tax-advantaged investment accounts for children in the US, created under the 2025 federal tax law known as the Working Families Tax Cuts. Legally, they are a type of traditional IRA created under new Section 530A of the tax code. Eligible US-citizen children born between January 1, 2025 and December 31, 2028 can receive a one-time $1,000 Treasury contribution, if the required election is made.IRSThe basic idea is to give children an investment asset early in life, allowing money to potentially grow through compound returns over many years. The Trump administration describes the programme as a way to give children a financial head start and encourage wider participation in investing.On July 4, as America marked its 250th birthday, the Dell Technologies founder and his wife Susan Dell gave $250 each to the first 25 million qualifying American children who sign up for a 'Trump Accounts’. Dell made the announcement on X, formerly Twitter, framing it as a "public-private partnership" that hands the next generation "a real stake in our economy." The couple had already pledged more than $6 billion to the programme back in December, so Saturday's post added a number to a commitment already made.“Today, on America's 250th birthday, Susan and I are celebrating by giving $250 each to the first 25 million qualifying American children who sign up for their @InvestAmerica24 @TrumpAccounts. This makes every child a shareholder in the greatest prosperity-creating engine the world has ever known—American capitalism. Through this public-private partnership, we're giving the next generation a real stake in our economy and a path to the American Dream: education, a first home, starting a business, and building lasting wealth. It unites us all in hope and optimism for every child's future. Happy 250th Birthday, America!,” the post then said.
Article Summary: Michael and Susan Dell donated $250 each to first 25 million Trump accounts. Trump Accounts are new, tax-advantaged investment accounts for children in the US, created under the 2025 federal tax law known as the Working Families Tax Cuts. The couple had already pledged more than $6 billion to the programme back in December.

Article Title: Nuuk partners with EPACK Durable to manufacture air fryers, air circulator fans in India
Article Text:
Focus on scaling high-quality products

EPACK expands SDA portfolio

Direct-to-consumer home appliance brand Nuuk has partnered with EPACK Durable Limited, one of India's leading original design manufacturers (ODMs) of consumer durables, to manufacture select small domestic appliances, including air circulator fans and air fryers. The partnership is aimed at strengthening Nuuk's manufacturing capabilities as it scales its product portfolio, while also expanding EPACK Durable's presence in the fast-growing small domestic appliances (SDA) segment. The companies said the collaboration combines Nuuk's design-led product development approach with EPACK Durable's manufacturing expertise.According to the companies, the agreement forms part of Nuuk's broader strategy to deepen its manufacturing ecosystem through partnerships with specialised production companies. The arrangement is expected to help the brand scale production while maintaining a focus on product quality, functionality and consumer-centric design.Nuuk, which has positioned itself as a new-age consumer appliances brand, said the collaboration will support its efforts to build products tailored to Indian consumers while strengthening its commitment to local manufacturing."Our partnership with EPACK Durable brings together our product and design orientation with deep manufacturing capabilities in the small domestic appliances category," said Gazal Kalra and Shalabh Gupta, co-founders of Nuuk.They added that the partnership would allow the company to expand with greater scale while remaining focused on quality and functionality.For EPACK Durable, the agreement broadens its engagement with emerging consumer appliance brands and further strengthens its SDA manufacturing portfolio. "We are pleased to partner with Nuuk and support the brand with our manufacturing capabilities across the consumer appliances segment," said Ajay DD Singhania, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of EPACK Durable. He said the company remains focused on building long-term relationships with brands through manufacturing scale, product capabilities and execution strength.EPACK Durable currently manufactures products across categories including room air conditioners, small domestic appliances, large domestic appliances and components through its manufacturing facilities in India. The company serves a range of consumer durable brands across the country.The companies said the partnership could create opportunities for broader collaboration across India's consumer appliances ecosystem in the future, combining product-led innovation with domestic manufacturing expertise as demand for locally manufactured appliances continues to grow.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos calls Mars a destination for humans, but wants to take Americans to Moon first, and in less than three years, as ...
Article Text:
'We'll go to Mars, but we need to go to the Moon first'

Jeff Bezos said Blue Origin plans to return its New Glenn rocket

Data centers in space

AI and work

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has outlined an ambitious vision for the future of space exploration, arguing that while Mars remains a long-term destination for humanity, the United States should focus on returning humans to the Moon first and establishing a permanent presence there. Speaking in an interview with Bret Baier on Fox News' "Special Report", the Amazon founder and Blue Origin executive chairman said the US must win the race against China to put humans back on the Moon. He expressed confidence that an American crewed lunar landing could happen by 2028, less than three years from now. "We have to beat China to the moon, and I believe we will beat China to the moon," Bezos said, adding that NASA and Blue Origin are working toward that goal.While Mars is often viewed as the next frontier for human exploration, Bezos said skipping the Moon would be a mistake. He described Earth's natural satellite as "a gift" because of its proximity and potential resources that could support deeper space missions. "We'll go to Mars. We'll do all the other things. But we need to go to the moon first," Bezos said during the interview. According to Bezos, establishing a sustainable lunar base could provide critical infrastructure for future exploration.He said routine cargo missions would be required to support a long-term human presence on the Moon, rather than treating lunar landings as one-off missions.Bezos argued that the Moon's resources could eventually play a significant role in supporting space development. He noted that lunar soil could potentially be used to manufacture solar cells, while oxygen produced on the Moon could serve as rocket propellant for missions travelling deeper into the solar system. "It won't just be a mission and leave," Bezos said. "It'll be a real sustainable lunar base."Bezos said Blue Origin plans to return its New Glenn rocket to flight in December, after an explosion during an engine test in May that Baier raised during the broadcast. The next flight will carry Blue Ring, a vehicle designed to move payloads into different orbits and farther into space, he said. He praised the team for repairing the launch pad.Asked about plans to raise launches from one pad from 12 to 50 a year, he said Blue Origin is building three more pads. His long-term target is far bigger: fly daily, then hourly, then every minute. He acknowledged that his own team thinks he is crazy, but said he has seen "crazy things" come true before.He said he has personally invested $28 billion in Blue Origin, which recently raised $10 billion from outside investors for the first time. He said an IPO could come several years from now.On the debate over data centers and electricity costs, Bezos pointed to Blue Origin's Project Sunrise. He said the company has applied to the Federal Communications Commission to launch more than 50,000 satellites that would act as orbital data centers, adding that there are good reasons to do so.Bezos predicted AI would deliver double-digit productivity gains across the economy. He said some families might get by on one income or a three-day workweek, and that this could make hiring harder as people choose to work less. Baier challenged him by citing the roughly 30,000 corporate roles Amazon has cut since late last year. Bezos said Amazon was in a "very special position" because it expanded its workforce substantially during the pandemic.At Prometheus, the startup where he is co-founder and co-CEO, Bezos said the goal is an "artificial general engineer" that helps people turn ideas into physical products. Asked whether AI is a bubble, he said it is very hard to know, but argued that the inventions survive even if the bubble bursts, as fiber-optic cable did after the internet boom. He urged a light regulatory touch while the technology is young, saying rules should target harmful uses rather than the technology itself.
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos says US must win race against China to put humans back on the Moon. He expressed confidence that an American crewed lunar landing could happen by 2028. Bezos said he has personally invested $28 billion in Blue Origin, which recently raised $10 billion from outside investors for the first time.

The latest cuts come as large technology companies continue to reassess staffing levels and spending plans amid growing investments in artificial intelligence and automation.
